info.name: Akamai Edge Diagnostics
info.description:
Tests Translate URL (sync) and URL Health Check (async, poll-based) against the Akamai Edge Diagnostics API.

Auth: EdgeGrid v1 — signing is performed at the COLLECTION level via a pre-request script that uses the four variables: akamai_host, akamai_client_token, akamai_client_secret, akamai_access_token.

Fill these variables in the collection's Variables tab from your .edgerc file before sending any request. Do not commit real credentials into a saved collection.

variable.description: Host from your .edgerc, no scheme. Example: akab-xxx-xxx.luna.akamaiapis.net
URL to evaluate. Override per-request if you want.
Auto-populated by the URL Health Check 'Submit' request. Used by the 'Poll' request.

exec: // Akamai EdgeGrid v1 request signer — collection-level pre-request
throw new Error('Akamai EdgeGrid credentials missing — fill akamai_host, akamai_client_token, akamai_client_secret, akamai_access_token in collection variables.');
// --- Build the canonical request that EdgeGrid signs ---
// Resolve the URL with all variables substituted, then strip scheme+host so we get path?query
// EdgeGrid signs the path-and-query portion only
const u = new URL(rawUrl.startsWith('http') ? rawUrl : 'https://' + host + rawUrl.replace(/^\/?/, '/'));
// Fallback: assume rawUrl is already a path
// Substitute variables in the body the same way Postman would when sending
// RFC4122-ish v4 UUID without crypto.randomUUID dependency
// auth-data (everything in Authorization header EXCEPT signature= )
// --- Body hash (POST/PUT only; max 131072 bytes per spec) ---
// method \t scheme \t host \t path?query \t canonicalized-headers \t content-hash \t auth-header
// canonicalized-headers is empty unless you've explicitly listed signed headers — we don't, so leave blank
contentHash,  // body hash, or '' for GET/DELETE
// Replace any prior Authorization header on this request

request.description:
Synchronous. Returns ARL details for the URL: typecode, cache key hostname, CP code, serial number, TTL, origin server, etc.

Response: 200 with JSON body. No polling.

exec: // Capture the request ID returned in the 202 response so the Poll request can use it.
// Akamai async responses typically include a 'requestId' field; some endpoints use 'id'.
console.log('[URL Health Check] requestId stored: ' + id);
console.warn('[URL Health Check] 202 received but no requestId / id field found in body. Inspect the response and update the test script.');
console.warn('[URL Health Check] expected 202, got ' + pm.response.code);

request.description:
Asynchronous. Stitches together CURL + DIG + GREP + MTR + Translate URL.

Response: 202 Accepted with a requestId. Use the '2b. Poll' request next, or expand the body with edgeIp / edgeLocation if you want a specific edge server to run from.

Polls the request submitted by '2a'.

If the response is 202 — still running, send again.
If 200 — results are ready in the body.

NOTE: confirm this exact path and the response field names from your tenant's API behavior on the first run. The Akamai docs sometimes shift between query-param polling and resource-style polling. If GET on this path 404s, try GET https://{{akamai_host}}/edge-diagnostics/v1/url-health-check?requestId={{url_health_check_request_id}}

item.name: DIAG 1. Identity Management — Get user profile

request.description:
Permission diagnostic — most API clients have this by default.

200: signing works AND client has at least basic API access. Edge Diagnostics 403 is then a SPECIFIC missing grant.
403: client has no API services granted at all — talk to your Akamai admin about granting services in general, not just Edge Diagnostics.

item.name: DIAG 2. Diagnostic Tools (legacy) — List ghost locations

request.description:
Permission diagnostic — Diagnostic Tools is the older sibling of Edge Diagnostics.

200: client can do diagnostics, just not via the Edge Diagnostics API. We could potentially fall back to this older API if Edge Diagnostics access is hard to get.
403: same gap as Edge Diagnostics — your client has no diagnostic API grants.

Permission diagnostic — also the Phase 2 (PM rule evaluator) API.

200: PAPI works. If Edge Diagnostics is blocked but PAPI isn't, we may want to skip ahead to Phase 2 instead of waiting for Edge Diagnostics permissions.
403: PAPI also blocked — same conversation with admin.
